page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute line. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware package bundles 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, but does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration.

The CPU cache topology integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set coverage includes vector extensions such as AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AVX-VNNI, as well as hardware cryptographic accelerations via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-threaded performance: the stress-ng single-core test reached 3056.38 points (top 25%), while single-threaded gzip compression scored 33.72 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression delivered 14.95 GB/sec (both in the top 25%). In Geekbench, text processing achieved top-tier performance at 2841.0 points (top 10%), alongside a single-core score of 1843.0.

Multithreaded operations demonstrate the constraints of a four-thread, two-physical-core profile. The Geekbench multi-core score reached 4251.0 (bottom 25%), and software compilation under Clang placed in the bottom 25% at 5597.0 points. While small-block cached memory bandwidth achieved 372.64 GB/sec, large uncached read and write bandwidth settled at 70.47 GB/sec and 41.18 GB/sec respectively. LLM inference shows viability for lightweight models, generating 217.72 tokens/sec on 135M models, but falls to 13.55 tokens/sec prompt processing on 7B models (bottom 10%). Redis operations reached 6.88 million SET operations per second, with static web serving throughput registering at 12.55 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is centered around memory density rather than raw parallel compute throughput. Because memory is abundant relative to the vCPU count, the instance is economically aligned with memory-bound workloads rather than compute-intensive compilations or heavy parallel processing. The primary trade-off involves trading lower multi-core computational throughput for high RAM capacity and local NVMe responsiveness. The instance is well matched for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, medium-sized transactional databases, memory-resident ETL pipelines, and text-heavy data processing.
description: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized cloud server within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Built on x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture at 2.0 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core), and a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD, without a GPU. The CPU features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core and text processing capabilities, scoring 3056.38 in stress-ng single-core and 2841.0 in Geekbench text processing, while multi-core workloads like Clang compilation are constrained by the physical core count. Memory bandwidth achieves 70.47 GB/sec on uncached reads, supporting 6.88 million Redis SET operations per second. With an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, vx1-m-4c-32g-240s provides efficient resource density for memory-bound tasks, including in-memory databases, Redis caching, ETL pipelines, and text analysis services.
